title: Retail inflation hits 21-month high of 5.54% as food prices bite
body: September retail inflation rose to 5.54% from 4.83% in August, a 21-month high. Food inflation jumped to 7.74% from 5.97%, and rural food inflation was 8.06%. Onions were up 108.09% year on year, ginger 62.85%, garlic 54.62% and silver jewellery 87.8%. The page says festive shopping is expected to get more expensive and that food is weighing most on household budgets, especially in rural areas. It adds that consumer durables, FMCG and auto makers have announced price increases that are expected to feed into inflation in the coming months.

title: UPI merchant fee postponed until after Diwali after trader protests
body: NPCI postponed a 0.4% merchant discount rate on some UPI payments that was due to start on October 15. It applies to eligible payments to merchants above Rs 2,000 and is capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. Person-to-person transfers and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000 are exempt. The article says the delay followed protests by trade associations in Kerala. Merchant bodies and fintech firms had also raised concerns about the impact in the peak shopping season. No new start date has been announced.

title: Shopkeepers and courts: the fight over the UPI fee before its planned October 15 start
body: This is the build-up to the fee that was later postponed. The page says the 0.4% fee would apply to payments above Rs 2,000 and cost a merchant Rs 300 on a Rs 1 lakh payment. A LocalCircles survey of over 32,000 businesses found only 17% would absorb a fee of 0.4% or more. Only 14% of surveyed consumers said they would keep paying by UPI if merchants added a fee on payments above Rs 2,000. Trade bodies withdrew a 'No UPI Day' protest after meeting the Finance Minister, and the Supreme Court declined to pause the framework. The government says about 96% of merchant payments are unaffected.

title: Quick-commerce survey: 60% say delivery and handling fees push bills above expectations
body: A festive-season survey found 60% of quick-commerce users say delivery, handling, small-cart or other fees often push their final bill above what they expected. Of those, 42% said 'very often' and 18% said 'often'. Another 43% rank low or no extra charges among their top three reasons for choosing a platform. The page says a free-delivery minimum of around Rs 199 is now common, and 27% of users spend under Rs 400 per order, so small fees hit them hardest. It notes that drip pricing is one of 13 dark patterns in the 2023 guidelines, and that the CCPA has imposed penalties of about Rs 1.1 crore on 47 e-commerce platforms.

title: Commercial LPG up again: Rs 62.50 to Rs 71.50 a cylinder; households spared
body: The 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder rose by Rs 62.50 to Rs 71.50 across major cities, the second consecutive monthly increase. Delhi is now Rs 2,810, Mumbai Rs 2,764.50, Kolkata Rs 2,954 and Patna Rs 3,100.50. Restaurants, food stalls, eateries and small industries bear the rise. The 14.2 kg domestic cylinder is unchanged since June 7 at Rs 942 in Delhi. The article blames higher crude prices and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Urban festive spending to fall 6% as households dip into savings
body: A LocalCircles survey of 67,000+ urban households projects festive spending falling about 6%, from Rs 2.10 lakh crore in 2025 to Rs 1.97 lakh crore. Households plan to spend roughly Rs 20,000 each, and 83% of those planning purchases will use savings for at least part of the cost. The survey calls the season 'more subdued'. The page notes the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7, its first rise in more than three and a half years. Clothing, footwear and accessories lead plans at 72%, while jewellery is at 6%.

title: Techarc: 69% of 2026 phones sell above launch price, mid-range up 24.4%
body: A Techarc study of 301 phones sold on Amazon and Flipkart found 69% of phones launched in 2026 sell above their launch price, and only 7% have become cheaper. Mid-range phones (Rs 12,000-25,000) are 24.4% costlier than last festive season, and entry phones (up to Rs 12,000) are 18.5% dearer. Only luxury phones above Rs 1,00,000 got cheaper, by 3.5%. Last year, entry-segment buyer activity fell to 0.72x during the festive window.

title: Renault launches Duster strong hybrid from Rs 16.99 lakh
body: Renault launched the Duster strong hybrid at introductory ex-showroom prices of Rs 16.99 lakh (Evolution), Rs 18.99 lakh (Techno) and Rs 19.49 lakh (Emotion). The prices apply to deliveries until December 31, 2026. Bookings are open at Rs 21,000 and deliveries start in November. An optional Renault Protect 360 package costs from Rs 89,900. The claimed mileage is 29 kpl, and the hybrid lacks the 360-degree camera and ADAS found on top petrol variants. The page reports company claims only and includes no customer reactions.

title: Hyundai launches Bayon SUV priced Rs 10 lakh to Rs 16 lakh
body: Hyundai launched the Bayon, a compact SUV positioned below the Creta, at Rs 10 lakh to Rs 16 lakh ex-showroom. It has a 1.5-litre petrol engine with 115 hp and a 6-speed manual or CVT. Features include dual 12.3-inch screens, ventilated front seats, a panoramic sunroof, Level 2 ADAS and six airbags. A factory CNG variant is planned for January. Rivals named are the Kia Seltos, Maruti Victoris, Honda Elevate and Skoda Kushaq. The page carries no customer reactions.

title: Hyderabad sweets up 20-25% before Diwali as sugar and nuts climb
body: Sweet prices in Hyderabad are up 20-25% ahead of Diwali. Gulab jamun and kalakand cost Rs 900-1,200/kg, and dry-fruit sweets Rs 1,800-2,900/kg. Sugar rose 17-20% in a couple of months, to Rs 60-70/kg from about Rs 45 in July and August. A sweet-shop manager said 'We have no option but to pass on the increased costs to customers.' A dry-fruit retailer expects prices to keep climbing, and the page notes that prices still rose even though the Centre cut GST on nuts from 12% to 5%.

title: Pistachio and date prices double, making Diwali gifting costlier in Mumbai
body: Wholesale pistachios have gone from Rs 900 to Rs 1,800 per kg and dates from Rs 250 to Rs 500. Almonds are Rs 1,100 (from Rs 800), and some dry fruits are up to 35% higher than last year. Traders blame geopolitical tensions, freight costs and a weaker rupee. Corporate gift buyers are working within fixed budgets, cutting basket weights or swapping in cheaper items. Demand for seeds as gifts has risen about 30% year on year, per CAIT's Shankar Thakkar, who expects Diwali sales to stay roughly flat with thinner margins.

title: SBI cuts free other-bank ATM transactions from October 1; LPG subsidy needs Aadhaar biometrics
body: From October 1, salary-package account holders at SBI get five free transactions a month at other banks' ATMs, down from 10. The limit counts both financial and non-financial transactions. Basic Savings account holders keep four free cash withdrawals, then pay Rs 15 plus GST each. Domestic LPG users must complete biometric Aadhaar authentication to get subsidised refills, otherwise they pay the market price. The report (IANS) also notes that the UPI fee framework, which customers are not charged, was then due on October 15. The article carries no public reactions.

title: Innodata lays off nearly 550 employees in India, job cuts reported in the Philippines
body: Nearly 550 Innodata employees in India were reportedly laid off. Innodata has not publicly confirmed that total. Staff said they lost access to official devices one by one during the workday. The termination emails then reached their personal accounts, naming 26 October 2026 as the last working day. Workers also lost access to the HR payroll app, so they could not download payslips. One employee said no one from HR had called. One employee said a WhatsApp group formed during the layoffs had 'almost 500 people' by late evening. The emails cited a 'ramp-down of the business assignment' and said the decision was 'not related to your individual performance.'

title: 52% of Indian CEOs plan workforce cuts as AI reshapes hiring (KPMG India CEO Outlook)
body: KPMG's 2026 India CEO Outlook surveyed 125 Indian CEOs between August 11 and September 21, 2026. It found that 52% plan workforce reductions in some areas, while 77% are hiring people with AI and technology skills. 87% are focused on retaining and retraining high-potential employees. 86% are reassessing the skills needed for entry-level roles. The article stresses these are CEOs' current plans, not confirmed job cuts. It says hiring and cuts may happen together, changing workforce composition more than total employment. The page quotes no workers, so it doesn't show how workers reacted.

title: Microsoft offers buyouts to about 60,000 employees, including in India
body: Microsoft announced a voluntary, time-limited buyout covering around 60,000 eligible employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce of 223,000 full-time employees as of June 30, 2026. Employees at level 70 and below in participating teams in India, the US, the UK and Canada are eligible. They have until early December to decide and would leave at year-end. Levels 64 and below get one week of base pay per six months of service, and severance for levels 67 and below is capped at 39 weeks of base pay. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said it gives staff 'a new choice' to transition now, with support. Microsoft cut 4,800 roles in July 2026, about 2.1% of its workforce. The article carries no employee reactions.

title: Amazon cuts 250 jobs after issuing an AI rulebook for software engineers
body: Amazon cut about 250 jobs in its devices and services unit, mostly software development roles. Another 1,000 people, mostly in the Stores unit, were laid off earlier in October. Employees were told by text and email early on a Wednesday. A day before the cuts, a September internal memo to engineers surfaced. It said token consumption, AI adoption rates and code changes don't necessarily show productivity. It also warned: 'We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind.' The company said it was making 'a difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles.' The page includes no worker quotes.

title: Cognizant reshapes workforce strategy with Project Leap
body: Cognizant revised its Project Leap restructuring cost estimate to $180–250 million, down from $230–320 million. The programme includes employee severance, which cost $46 million this quarter. Headcount at 30 September 2026 was 3,59,900, up 3,200 on the quarter. Voluntary attrition in technology services was 12.6%. Over 50% of code is now AI-assisted. Bookings fell 7% year on year, prompting a cut to full-year revenue guidance. The page has no quotes from employees or executives. HRKatha's own analysis calls it a 'dual challenge' of restructuring and growth.

title: Indian IT hiring in Q2: HCLTech adds 6,450 employees as Wipro loses 6,716
body: At the end of September, TCS had 598,056 employees, up from 593,798. Infosys had 332,542, up 4,480. HCLTech had 230,339, up 6,450, after taking on 6,136 freshers this quarter against 1,056 in June. Wipro fell 6,716 (about 2.8%) to 236,328. Attrition was 13.3% at TCS, 12.7% at Infosys, 12.8% at HCLTech and 13.8% at Wipro. TCS's CHRO called its attrition 'stable' and said the company is focusing on upskilling and hiring for critical skills. The article notes that attrition definitions differ by company, so the figures aren't strictly comparable. It carries no employee commentary.

title: Festive cheer: Diwali bonuses and pay hikes across India
body: The Union Cabinet approved a 3-percentage-point DA/DR hike, from 60% to 63%, effective retrospectively from 1 July 2026. It covers 48 lakh employees and 68 lakh pensioners and costs Rs 10,016 crore a year. Mumbai's BMC announced a Rs 33,000 Diwali bonus for over 93,000 employees, Rs 2,000 more than last year. Goa gave 30 days' emoluments, capped at Rs 6,908. Rajasthan's 3% DA rise and bonus are reportedly under preparation but unconfirmed. In the private sector, the article notes only that MITS Group's chairman gifted four Kia Sonet SUVs to high performers. The page has no worker reactions.

title: Ahead of Jio IPO, Reliance releases October salary 15 days early to encourage investment
body: Per Bloomberg, Reliance paid October salaries about 15 days early. It also contacted most employees across group companies about investing in the Jio Platforms IPO. Teams asked whether employees or their family members have trading accounts and encouraged those without one to open one. The IPO is up to ₹30,200 crore, with an employee quota of up to ₹500 crore at a 5% discount. Jio has 74,822 employees out of 419,911 across Reliance. Employees were not told why salaries came early. The page has no other reactions.

title: BT Big Story: No jobs, no security — the crisis facing India's educated youth
body: Youth (15+) unemployment was 15.1% in the August 2026 PLFS, about three times the overall rate of 5%. On the NCS portal, 28.9 million jobseekers were registered against 1.76 million active vacancies as of July 2026. Indeed's survey of 2,633 job seekers found 70% say a first job is harder to get than three to five years ago. A Delhi employment exchange official said, 'For every one job vacancy, we send 20 potential candidates.' A 23-year-old graduate works in a packaging factory while preparing for police exams. Indeed India said employers want upskilled freshers with soft skills. The Chief Economic Adviser asked the private sector to invest, hire and pay fairly, and said AI should complement rather than displace labour.

title: IIT Madras white paper warns AI puts entry-level workers at risk
body: The paper cites a 2026 Cognizant-Pearson survey of 750 HR leaders. It found 37% of entry-level tasks in India are already performed by AI, against 33% globally. It states that India's top IT companies added a net 17 employees in the first nine months of fiscal 2026. PLFS 2025 shows 25% of youth aged 15-29 are not in employment, education or training. IIT Madras researcher Gokul S Krishnan said: 'AI taking over a task does not automatically mean a job disappears.' The authors say new AI roles don't guarantee displaced workers can move into them. They recommend redesigning entry-level roles so workers learn to supervise and correct AI.

title: Can AI fast-track your next promotion?
body: Scaler's India AI Workforce Report 2026 (11,444 professionals) reports a 147% average salary increase among professionals after AI upskilling. The article notes this does not prove upskilling caused the rise. A survey of 1,200 AI decision-makers found 67% of businesses tie AI skills to promotion criteria and 50% include them in performance evaluations. In TeamLease EdTech's study of 14,316 professionals, 64% of employed respondents who upskilled said it definitely influenced their appraisal outcome. Experts say judgement matters more than tool familiarity. TeamLease EdTech's CEO said appraisals should measure outcomes, not how often employees use AI.

title: AI will change workforce composition; GCCs to add 1.4 million jobs by 2031, says report
body: An Embark report says India's GCCs employ about 2.3 million people and could reach 3.3-3.7 million by 2031, a net gain of up to 1.4 million. AI-led automation, slower backfilling and role consolidation could reduce demand for routine jobs by 400,000-500,000. Of 100 GCC leaders surveyed, 92% have moved beyond selective AI adoption, but realised productivity gains remain below 15%. Shared and collaborative spaces are expected to rise from 27% to 55% of workplace allocation by 2031. The page includes no worker reactions.

title: Instagram announces 'Features', a 90-minute long-form video test, with no India date
body: Instagram announced on October 26, 2026 that it is testing a long-form format called Features. Selected creators can upload horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes, aimed at podcasters, interviewers and comedians who now post long videos on YouTube. Testing has started in Brazil and is expanding to a select group in the US. The page says Instagram has not announced an India launch date. It also says Instagram has not confirmed a revenue-sharing model. Instagram is testing 'Clips as Reels', which links short highlights back to the full video, and it is developing a 'Series' feature. The page quotes no creator reactions.

title: Piyush Goyal's 'nobody in India will tell you it's 5 o'clock' remark triggers overwork backlash online
body: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal told an India-Netherlands Business Forum on October 27 that Indians do not track office hours or weekends. Critics said this glorifies overwork and burnout. One critical Instagram comment, 'Overworking isn't a badge of honour', got more than 3,000 likes. Some X users called it a 'slave mindset' and asked whether long hours and low pay should be India's selling point. RPG Group chairman Harsh Goenka defended the remark, saying Indians' willingness to work late gives the country an edge.

title: Lahore kids' qawwali on 'Alfaaz' wins hearts in India, nicknamed 'little Nusrats'
body: A clip of young qawwali singers from Lahore's Sur Taal Music Academy performing the Punjabi song 'Alfaaz' with Norwegian performer William Gamborg has spread across the India-Pakistan border. It has reportedly crossed 49.2 million views. An Indian user compared the kids' singing to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan's, and the nickname 'little Nusrats' stuck. Viewers say it 'lives in my head rent free'. Others call it 'obsessed' viewing and say the kids 'nailed it'. One wished they could join the group from India.

title: 19-year-old Vrindavan preacher becomes 'Pookie Baba' / 'Gen Z Baba' on Instagram and X
body: Clips of 19-year-old Bhagwat Katha narrator Shashwat Acharya went viral on Instagram and X. People were drawn to his youthful looks, curly hair and clean-shaven appearance. Users made memes and joking comments, and nicknamed him 'Gen Z Baba' and 'Pookie Baba'. The 'Pookie Baba' tag had earlier been used for another preacher, Aniruddhacharya Ji Maharaj. The article gives no view or follower numbers.

title: Indian chef in the US posts Diwali loneliness reel; Instagram replies 'you chose to go for money'
body: Kartik Chauhan, a chef who has spent four years in the US, posted an Instagram video of his empty, quiet neighbourhood on Diwali night. He said his luxury home and Mustang cannot replace family and friends, and that money brings happiness only while you spend it. Some commenters had little sympathy. One said he went abroad to earn money and should be grateful, because 'you can't have everything at once'. Another asked what was stopping him from returning to India. The headline's jab is that he is unhappy even with a Mustang.

title: Ahmedabad 'grocery store rave' video goes viral, internet split
body: Youngsters danced to DJ beats inside a grocery store (Food Square India) in Ahmedabad on October 27, and videos spread online. The article gives no attendance or view figures. Some users loved it, writing 'Are you serious this is awesome'. Others were baffled and asked whether music sessions are even allowed in a grocery shop. One joked that Ahmedabad allows random events like this but not alcohol.

title: Mumbai's BMC installs AI cameras that issue audio warnings to people littering
body: BMC's G/North ward put AI cameras at Gajanan Vatika in Mahim. When the system spots suspected littering, it plays a loudspeaker warning asking the person to stop. BMC shared a demo video on X and plans more cameras at other Mumbai locations. It did not say whether repeat offenders will be fined. Reaction was mostly positive, with some joking the cameras should go inside BMC offices. Others said warnings alone won't stop dumping and asked for penalties, and one asked, 'Isn't this very basic? Why are we spending money for this?'

title: 'Thanda paani mat peena': a woman fan's motherly advice to 15-year-old Vaibhav Suryavanshi goes viral
body: After India's third T20I against New Zealand in Wellington on October 27, a woman spectator who said she was from Ballia told 15-year-old Vaibhav Suryavanshi not to drink cold water and to warm it first. He smiled and replied 'Achha ji, theek hai'. The clip went viral. The article says it won hearts online, but it quotes no individual reactions. Suryavanshi is from Samastipur, Bihar, and became the youngest IPL player in April 2025.

title: Diljit Dosanjh tells people to 'check the news first' over Delhi concert postponement rumours
body: Reports said Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi concert was postponed after Delhi Police reportedly denied permission over security concerns. He went on an Instagram live and told people to find out the facts before posting reels, tweets and debates. He said the October 30 Delhi show was on. The article calls the postponement claims speculation. It describes a wave of reels, tweets and newsroom debates, and includes no statement from police or organisers.

title: Young river cleaner Bittu Tabahi filmed as a man throws garbage over him; internet says 'we lack civic sense'
body: Bittu Tabahi, a 20-year-old environmentalist, was cleaning the Ajnar river after Dussehra and Navratri, which he said made it worse. A man on a bridge appeared to throw a bag of garbage toward him. He posted the video on Instagram, saying people keep littering despite months of effort. Commenters said people lack civic sense and empathy, and one said she was proud of him but sad about the situation. Another tagged the Madhya Pradesh police and asked for heavy penalties for littering in the river.

title: Viral clip of a new car scratched the morning after celebration sparks 'jealousy' debate
body: A 13-second clip shared on X on October 24 shows a man breaking a coconut before his new Maruti car at night, with relatives celebrating. The next morning the car is allegedly covered in scratches, and the post blames jealousy. The article says the location is unspecified and the claim is unverified. Several users shared similar stories of damaged cars, and some blamed jealousy. Others suggested a parking dispute and said people should not buy cars without parking space.

title: Jailer 2 opens huge in Kerala, but Mohanlal fans are upset about his trimmed role
body: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 earned ₹12.50 crore in Kerala on Day 1, per Sacnilk. That is the second-highest opening-day gross in Kerala's history, behind Empuraan (₹14 crore) and ahead of Leo (₹12 crore). The page puts India Day 1 gross at ₹70.25 crore and worldwide at ₹125.25 crore. Many Mohanlal fans in Kerala were disappointed after the first shows because his role was short. Reports said scenes shown in the trailer were cut. His costume designer posted that three looks were removed and that he would not work on a Jailer 3. Some fans accused the makers of shrinking Mohanlal's part to keep the focus on Rajinikanth.

title: Jailer 2 first-day crowds love Rajinikanth and Hrithik's cameo but argue over the second half
body: Sacnilk's first-day-first-show roundup calls the reaction mixed-to-positive. Fans enjoyed Rajinikanth's screen presence, the comedy, the interval sequence and Anirudh's background score. Critics of the film said the screenplay lost momentum, the villains were weak and some elevation scenes felt familiar. In a small sample of online ratings, 7.1% gave 2/5 or below, 50.0% gave above 2 to 3/5, 28.6% gave above 3 to 4/5 and 14.3% gave above 4 to 5/5. The page itself warns that this small sample is not the audience consensus. The split depends on whether viewers wanted a celebration of the star or a stronger story.

title: Drishyam 3: Hindi finale outruns the Malayalam original at the box office, and viewers compare the two
body: Sacnilk compares the two versions. The Hindi Drishyam 3 (released 2 Oct) shows India net ₹315.25 Cr and worldwide gross ₹489.74 Cr (as of 11 days). The Malayalam one (released 21 May) shows ₹110.49 Cr India net and ₹239.83 Cr worldwide gross, and is labelled Blockbuster. Overseas grosses are nearly identical, so the Hindi lead comes from Indian collections. Viewers praised the Hindi version's suspense, interval and climax, and said Vijay's journey ended well. The Malayalam version was praised for emotional weight and Mohanlal's controlled performance. Some found its pacing slow and familiar. The writer's view is that the Hindi film met more of what people wanted from a final chapter.

title: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to win Asian Games cricket gold
body: India won the Asian Games men's cricket final against Pakistan in Nisshin, Japan, by 19 runs, scoring 211/6 in 20 overs. Pakistan finished on 192/6 chasing 212. Abhishek Sharma made 61 off 28 balls with 7 sixes, and Tilak Varma was unbeaten on 51 off 22. Washington Sundar's bowling was named as a key contributor, and India's bowlers stopped Pakistan completing what would have been a record chase. The page has no fan quotes. It is a clear India-Pakistan win for people who follow the rivalry.

title: West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the Hyderabad T20I, run-fest levels series 2-2
body: In the fourth T20I at Hyderabad, West Indies made 247/3 and won by 24 runs. Shai Hope hit 102 not out off 50 balls and was Player of the Match. India fell short on 223/9 in 19.3 overs, chasing 248. Sanju Samson top-scored with 56 and Tilak Varma made 43. Keemo Paul took 5 wickets. The result left the five-match series level at 2-2. The page carries no fan reaction. Earlier search results suggested a third-umpire stumping call on Naman Dhir divided fans on X, but I could not open that page.

title: Rain washes out the Bengaluru decider as India–West Indies series ends 2-2
body: The fifth T20I at the Chinnaswamy Stadium on 17 October was abandoned with India on 118/5 after 7.4 overs. Ishan Kishan made 30 off 10 balls. A revised target of 84 in five overs was set for West Indies, but more rain stopped play. The page says West Indies had a series run rate of 10.98, the highest by a Full Member team in a bilateral T20I series. They also hit 105 sixes across the five matches. The writer calls the washout frustrating for players and supporters. The page has no direct fan quotes.

title: Udta Teer: audiences laugh at Ayushmann's amnesiac spy comedy, then argue about the second half
body: Udta Teer opened on a Friday, with Ayushmann Khurrana as a Pakistani spy who loses his memory and believes he is Indian. The page gives no box office figures. It samples about 15 posts from X, Instagram and Reddit and mentions one two-star review. Viewers praised the humour, Khurrana, Rahul Bose's largely wordless role and Mukul Dev's final role, and some called it paisa-vasool. Many said the second half dropped, the romance did not work and the climax was illogical, and one called it a snoozefest. A viral clip from a promotion at the Attari-Wagah border, where a Pakistani-side loudspeaker drowned out the stars, added to the buzz.

title: Ramayana advance booking hits a snag as distributors ask for a bigger revenue share
body: Advance booking for Ramayana: Part 1 was meant to start on Dussehra, 20 October, but only a few theatres opened bookings because distributors and exhibitors disagreed on terms. Distributors wanted 60% of net ticket revenue in week 1 (usual 52.5%), 50% in week 2 (usual 45%) and 40% in week 3 (usual 37.5%). Exhibitors were reluctant and talks were continuing. INOX Korum Mall in Thane and AMB Cinemas in Bengaluru were among the few venues selling tickets. A sidebar headline says the deadlock reportedly ended later, but I could not confirm the details from this page.

title: Ramayana's IMAX shows drive pre-sales while ticket prices raise eyebrows
body: Per Sacnilk, Ramayana's advance gross is ₹11.11 crore including blocked seats, with more than two lakh tickets sold in five days. IMAX is about 25% of advance collections from 3.8% of screenings, averaging about 170 tickets per show against 35 for regular shows. The Hindi version is about 87% of collections. Maharashtra leads with ₹2.44 crore, then Delhi ₹2.24 crore and Karnataka ₹1.71 crore. The page's price figures conflict (₹1,095 in the headline, an IMAX average of ₹380 in the text), so check the real prices before quoting them. The strong IMAX demand suggests many people are paying extra for the big-screen experience.

title: Ramayana's early advance sales are set against Adipurush's weak memory
body: Sacnilk compares Ramayana (release 5 Nov) at 14 days out with Adipurush's final opening-day advances. Ramayana shows ₹7.25 Cr advance gross (₹5.35 Cr excluding block seats) and 1.29 lakh+ tickets sold. Adipurush shows ₹26.40 Cr excluding block seats and 10.74 lakh tickets, and the page says these are not like-for-like snapshots. Early demand is concentrated in the Hindi market, strong in Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR, and premium recliner seats sold out in some Mumbai cinemas. The page says Adipurush opened strongly, then declined steeply after criticism of its dialogue, effects and characters. There are no audience quotes, but the comparison shows how wary viewers are of a big mythological film after Adipurush.

title: Delhi Police first deny, then clear Diljit Dosanjh's 30 October concert at JLN Stadium
body: Delhi Police denied permission on Thursday, citing threat-related inputs, security concerns and festive-season law-and-order commitments. After meeting organiser BookMyShow on Friday, they reversed the decision. BookMyShow Live said police asked for extra safety, traffic and crowd-management measures. Diljit, who was in the US, posted on Instagram: "Now let's meet on 30th in Delhi," and urged people to "Find out the facts first before jumping to conclusions." The Delhi show opens his Aura World Tour, with Indore, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Chandigarh to follow. The page carries no fan reactions, only Diljit's own video.

title: Box office check, mid-October: Drishyam 3 leads while Hanuman Ansh runs long and Sigma stays under ₹9 crore
body: The report puts Drishyam: The Conclusion at ₹501.80 crore worldwide gross on Day 12 (citing The Times of India), with trackers showing India net in the low-to-mid ₹320 crore range. Its Tuesday collection rose 41.7% on the previous day. Hanuman Ansh stands at ₹438.40 crore worldwide gross. Its Day 68 collection was ₹1.30 crore. Baththa is nearing ₹26 crore gross after ₹1.22 crore on Day 13, and Sigma is below ₹9 crore, which makes it the weak performer on the list. The page has no direct audience quotes and says its figures are provisional.

title: FASTag annual local pass: ₹1,500 a year for people living near toll plazas
body: From November 1, 2026 NHAI will offer a concessional annual FASTag local pass to private, non-commercial vehicle owners who live within 20 km of a national highway toll plaza. It costs ₹1,500 a year at plazas outside municipal or local town limits and ₹3,000 within them. The current monthly local pass costs ₹360, or ₹4,320 a year, so the annual pass could save ₹2,820 at an outside-limits plaza. Living nearby does not qualify someone automatically, and the pass is not available on closed-user-fee highways or where a service road exists. The page quotes no commuter reactions; the Road Transport Ministry says the move makes 'regular travel more affordable' for people living near toll plazas.

title: November 1 changes: pension life certificates, audit-case ITR deadline, GST and LPG review
body: Several rules shift on November 1. Pensioners below 80 can submit their Jeevan Pramaan life certificate from November 1, generally until November 30, and missing the window can temporarily halt pension payments. For Assessment Year 2026-27, the deadline for audit-subject taxpayers moved from October 31 to November 21, 2026, and salaried individuals outside those categories are not covered. A Cabinet-approved disability pension reform would lower the minimum threshold from 80% to 40%, with Rs 375 a month proposed for beneficiaries below 80 and Rs 625 for those 80 and above, but it is not expected from November 1. The page says no LPG price change had been announced as of October 29. It also notes that several banks have recently revised fixed deposit rates, with no figures given.

title: Match Group–Ipsos survey: Indian singles have hundreds of online friends but feel lonely offline
body: A Match Group and Ipsos survey of 1,000 singles aged 18 to 45 in metro and tier-1 cities found about 35% feel lonely all the time. About 58% socialise widely online but feel lonely offline, and about 55% are too tired after work to meet or talk with anyone. About 64% put studies and jobs ahead of their social life, and about 72% want a few deep connections rather than many casual friends. About 40% use a dating app, and about 63% of those say apps have reduced their loneliness. About 60% worry about safety in online dating. Respondents say work exhaustion, not a lack of chances to socialise, is the main driver. The page notes the survey was run by a dating-app company with a commercial interest.

title: Caller names on your screen from November 1, plus stricter spam-call rules
body: A DoT circular dated 13 October 2026 tells operators to show caller names (CNAP) on 4G and higher networks from 1 November 2026. Spam-call rules that went live around 18 October let operators flag likely spam numbers, and five or more flagged numbers in ten days triggers graded action. Customers set to FULLY BLOCK move to BLOCK PROMO within fifteen days. Automated calls must be declared to the operator from about 17 November, with a termination charge of up to ₹0.05 per minute. The page is an explainer and quotes no user reactions.

title: Retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September; food inflation hits 7.74%
body: Retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, and food inflation rose to 7.74% from 5.97%, per MoSPI data. Rural inflation was 6.08% against 4.88% in urban areas. Potatoes, tomatoes and lady's finger were cheaper than a year earlier. ISB Professor Prasanna Tantri welcomed the RBI's rate hike on X but said the central bank was late and that 'We cannot sustain zero real interest rates'.

title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%, first hike since February 2023; EMIs set to rise
body: The RBI raised the repo rate 25 basis points from 5.25% to 5.50%, its first hike since February 2023, and moved to 'calibrated tightening' by a 4–2 vote. On a Rs 50 lakh, 25-year home loan, a rise in the lending rate from 7.50% to 7.75% lifts the EMI from about Rs 36,950 to Rs 37,766, an extra Rs 817 a month. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts are off the table in the near term. HDFC Bank expects another 50–75 bps of hikes. BankBazaar's Adhil Shetty advised borrowers not to plan on lower EMIs, and ANAROCK's Anuj Puri said higher EMIs could push affordable-housing buyers to defer purchases.

title: Gold near ₹1.35 lakh per 10 g ahead of Dhanteras: buy now or wait?
body: On October 18, 24K gold was ₹1,47,660 and 22K ₹1,35,350 per 10 grams in most metros, slightly higher in Delhi at ₹1,47,810 and ₹1,35,500. These are indicative rates that exclude 3% GST, making charges and wastage. The page says buyers are weighing whether to buy now or wait, and that recent dips offer an opportunity but do not mean prices have bottomed. It advises households to compare city-wise rates and final bills. It cites festive and wedding demand, the rupee and US rate expectations as drivers. A separate NewsBytes snippet in search results says gold is down 26% since January, but I could not open that page, so treat it as unconfirmed.

title: White-collar hiring up only 2% in September; fresher hiring barely moves; Delhi and Mumbai fall 6%
body: The Naukri JobSpeak Index was 3,053 in September against 3,002 a year earlier, up 2%. AI/ML hiring jumped 20% and auto rose 11%, while IT/software services, pharma/biotech and FMCG each fell 4%. By city, Hyderabad rose 9%, Chennai 6% and Bengaluru and Kolkata 4% each, while Delhi-NCR and Mumbai each fell 6%. The article opens by saying white-collar hiring 'remained mostly steady'. It quotes no job-seekers.

title: Delhi winter plan from Nov 1: half the office staff at home, non-BS6 outside vehicles barred, parking fees doubled
body: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced the winter measures on October 20, 2026. Non-BS6 vehicles registered outside Delhi may not enter from November 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027, and EVs, CNG and essential-service vehicles are exempt. Fuel stations will not supply fuel to vehicles without a valid PUC certificate. Parking fees at authorised municipal sites double, with DMRC lots excluded. A 50% work-from-home arrangement applies across public and private offices, with MCD offices running 8:30 am to 5 pm and Delhi government offices 10 am to 6:30 pm. The page reports no public reaction. A Cars24 explainer says over 10 lakh non-BS6 vehicles are in the affected region, per WION estimates. Another outlet gives different end dates for the work-from-home order, so check the official notification.

title: Onion prices up 108% in a year: kitchen costs bite as ginger, garlic and lemon also climb
body: September price data shows onions up 108.09% year on year, the steepest rise among tracked items, with ginger up 62.85%, garlic 54.62% and lemons 36.41%. Potatoes, tomatoes, lady's fingers and coconuts were cheaper than a year earlier. The article says the increases 'could make everyday cooking more expensive for households'. DBS economist Radhika Rao expects further food and fuel pressure in the coming months. The page has no direct consumer quotes.
